findings.title: The knowledge check is written, keyed and briefed by the session it examines
findings.target: Section 4 step 4 (probe.json), section 5 step 2, amendment 1 step 3
findings.argument: Follow one field. Section 4.4 has the builder write probe.json, with its twelve questions and answer keys (lines 50-51). Amendment 1 makes the builder and the expert one child (lines 129-130, 137-138), so the child writes its own exam and its own keys, then sits it with the pack and the keys in the same window. The grader is 'a checker' (line 61), which is a level-2 helper of that same child (line 21), so the child also writes the grader's brief. Nothing outside the child touches the check: the coordinator never reads packs (line 19, row 11 line 174), and gate A checks only schema, the 95 % figure, coverage and size (lines 52-53). A 10-of-12 pass therefore shows that the child can read its own answer key. This check is the only point in the design that tests the owner's condition 'so it has the knowledge to be called a proper expert', and as written it certifies nothing. The same holds for the replacement experts in lines 62 and 143.
findings.smallest_fix: Move probe authorship out of the child. After gate A, a checker whose brief is a fixed file the child cannot edit writes probe.json and its keys into its own folder. It works from the coordinator-written question list (see R1-07) and the confirmed cards, and the child sees only the questions. The schema script grades the card ids and the checker grades the prose. If that is not wanted, delete the knowledge check and say plainly that gate A coverage is the only test. A self-set exam should not be kept as if it were a gate.

findings.title: The 300,000-token ceiling is called the exception, but the protocol's own sizes make it the likely path
findings.target: Amendment 1 step 5; section 4 step 4 pack size; section 5 step 3 review inputs; section 6 refuter
findings.argument: Add up one child's window before its review starts. Fixed prefix: about 20-60k. Cards and 'the passages that matter' returned by helpers (line 132): about 15-40k. Five to eight primary sources read in the original by the child itself (lines 50, 133), at about 10-30k per paper: 50-240k. Writing pack.md at 60-90k (line 49): the content of the write call stays in the window, so another 60-90k, plus edits. Probe and state-of-field: about 5k. The review then adds our work: the problem sheet plus a fixed list of protocols, results and designs per field (lines 63-65), about 30-100k. Before the review that is about 150-470k; with the review inputs, about 190-530k. The ceiling at 300k (line 142) is therefore crossed in a large share of fields, not 'the exception' (line 143). The refuter that holds 'the packs' of three leads (line 82) starts at 180-270k before it reads a single review. Nobody measures a child's window either: a session does not see its own token count, and no outside reader is named.
findings.smallest_fix: Remove the word 'exception' and size the protocol so that the fallback always works. Gate A requires pack.md, the must-read sections and the field's fixed review files to fit together under about 200k for a fresh session. The pilot field measures how often the ceiling binds. The window is read from the harness's session records by the watcher script in R1-04, not judged by the child. The refuter gets the three fields' review.json and the cited cards, not whole packs.

findings.title: Four separate recovery paths each restore the builder/expert split that amendment 1 withdrew, each with different rules
findings.target: Section 5 steps 2 and 5, amendment 1 step 5, amendment 2 row 10
findings.argument: Amendment 1 withdraws the split into a builder and a fresh expert (line 129). Four rules then bring it back by separate doors. (a) A failed probe means 'a new expert is started from it' (line 62). (b) A pack gap found during review goes back to stage A and 'a new expert is started from the repaired pack' (lines 72-73). Under amendment 1 the child is its own builder and could research the gap itself, so (b) discards a filled window for nothing. (c) The ceiling hands over to 'a fresh session [that] reads the pack' (lines 142-143). (d) After a crash 'a session can be started again from its folder' (line 173). None of these says whether the new session reads the must-reads, retakes the probe, or is marked in the ledger. What a hand-over loses is also left unsaid: everything read in the original but not written to a card, and the child's judgment of where sources disagree. A crash before pack.md exists leaves only cards.jsonl, so (d) restores files, not an expert. 'Started again from its folder' is a wish unless the folder holds a pack.
findings.smallest_fix: Replace the four with one rule. A child that cannot go on, whether from the ceiling, a crash or a failed probe, is replaced by a fresh session that reads the frozen pack.md and the must-read sections, retakes the probe, and has its review marked 'from pack' in the ledger. If the crash comes before a pack exists, the field restarts from its cards. A gap found during review is researched by the same child with its helpers, under the ceiling. Delete line 73's 'new expert'.

findings.title: Nobody reads the heartbeat: the coordinator is idle between turns, and a stall, a repair request or sleep goes unseen
findings.target: Amendment 2 rows 9 and 11; rule 7.7; section 5 step 5
findings.argument: After the coordinator starts a wave it ends its turn, and from then on it does nothing. Each check in this group has no runner. The heartbeat is a line in the ledger (line 172), but no reader and no time to read it are named. 'Reported' (line 103) has no recipient. A repair request is a file (line 72, 'files are the only interface', line 91), and nobody is in a turn to open it. 'The coordinator keeps the PC awake' (line 172) cannot be done by a session that is not in a turn. If the children finish, or end their turn waiting on a repair, the PC sleeps after 15 minutes and the programme stands still until the owner returns: the silent wait that rule 7.7 forbids. 'A late field is restarted or dropped' (line 172) also never says to stop the stalled session first, so a replacement makes four children, or the stalled one keeps spending tokens. The coordinator hand-over at 200k (line 174) is a self-written state summary. The owner's own summary check found most of those overtaken in their kept tail, and no file-derived state exists to replace it.
findings.smallest_fix: One mechanism in place of four wishes. After starting a wave, the coordinator launches one background watcher script that holds a keep-awake for the wave. The script polls the child folders and the session records and writes status.json, where each field has a state, a token count, the age of its last heartbeat and any repair or done file. It exits on the first event (done, repair request, heartbeat older than the time box, window over the ceiling, programme usage over the cap), and its exit re-invokes the coordinator. The coordinator stops a stalled session before it replaces one. The coordinator reads only status.json, so a 200k hand-over is 'read status.json', not a summary. Test on the pilot whether a background command keeps the machine awake.

findings.title: The token cap is read only between waves, cannot stop a wave in flight, and is split across roles that no longer exist
findings.target: Rule 7.4, section 9, amendment 2 rows 8 and 14, part C last bullet
findings.argument: Usage is read before and after each wave (line 97). Three children with up to six helpers each (line 171), 18 agents at once, can pass the cap in the middle of a wave, and 'at the cap the programme stops' (line 98) names no one who stops running children. The weekly limit has already been exhausted once in exactly this way (direction lines 107-110). Section 9 divides the 10 % into half for packs and a quarter for experts (line 122), but amendment 1 put pack and expert in one session, so neither share can be measured or enforced. The same applies to 'a token ceiling per pack and per expert' (line 96). The 'total cap' of row 8 has no number. The ledger asks each session and agent to report its own tokens (lines 100-101), which no session can see. The count of runs is also missing: seven fields, up to three independent second experts (line 140), the single-session control field (lines 189-191), a refuter and the checkers come to about eleven child-sized runs, four waves or more, against a cap set before the pilot. The pilot (row 14) is the right tool, but nothing turns its number into a stop. Separately, waves of three children plus the coordinator make four sessions, while rule 7.4 says 'at most three sessions at once' (line 96).
findings.smallest_fix: Delete the half/quarter/quarter split and the per-pack/per-expert ceilings. Add one admission rule: a wave starts only if the remaining programme budget is at least 1.5 × (the pilot's measured tokens per field) × (fields in the wave). Tokens come from a script over the harness's session records, not from self-reports. At the cap the R1-04 watcher exits and the coordinator stops the wave's sessions. List the runs (including second experts and the control) in the wave plan. Say whether the coordinator counts toward the three-session limit.

findings.title: The shared ledger and the shared source register break 'one writer per folder', cannot be shared across per-child branches, race on claims, and defeat second-expert independence
findings.target: Rule 7.1; rule 7.6; amendment 2 rows 6, 7 and 9; amendment 1 step 4
findings.argument: Rule 7.1 and row 6 say nobody writes outside its own folder and that each child works on its own branch (lines 90, 169). Two shared files contradict that. (1) LEDGER.jsonl, which every session and agent writes (lines 100-101, 111), and to which row 9 adds heartbeats. (2) The source register (line 170), which every helper in every field checks and writes. Three children on three branches need three worktrees, because one shared checkout would have each branch switch move the others' files, and the protocol says neither. In separate worktrees each child sees its own copy of both files, so the register de-duplicates nothing across fields and the coordinator sees no heartbeat until it merges. In a shared directory, two helpers that check-then-claim the same paper both find it free, and concurrent appends from up to 18 agents can interleave. Worst, the register defeats amendment 1 step 4. The second expert's helpers would find the first expert's sources 'claimed' and skip them, yet the second expert must read the same field independently (lines 140-141, row 3 line 161).
findings.smallest_fix: Remove rules rather than add locks. Delete the source register (row 7). Field boundaries come from coordinator-written question lists (R1-07), and after each wave a script counts duplicate DOIs across cards.jsonl files as a ledger measure. Each session writes its ledger lines in its own folder (fields/<n>/ledger.jsonl), and the watcher concatenates them into status.json. State that each child runs in its own git worktree.

findings.title: Each child writes its own question list from a file that carries the owner's hopes, and nobody checks it
findings.target: Section 4 step 1, gate A, amendment 1 step 4, amendment 2 row 7
findings.argument: The builder, which under amendment 1 is the child, writes the field's questions 'from the direction file' (line 36). Gate A then checks that 'the pack covers the field's questions' (line 53), so the child sets its own scope and is graded against it. No gate checks the list itself, and the first gate, 'direction approved' (line 93), comes before any list exists. The direction file states the owner's hopes outright ('the graphics card may be under-used and the architecture's assumptions may be wrong', direction lines 6-7; 'none of them ruled out', line 15). Section 5 step 3 says the expert must not be given the owner's hopes (lines 64-65), and row 2's 'neutral briefs' (line 160) depends on the same separation. Row 7's 'field boundaries fixed in the question lists' (line 170) cannot hold either: the lists are written by children that never talk to each other (line 21), in different waves. The second expert works 'from the same question list' (line 141), which the first expert wrote, so it inherits the first expert's framing.
findings.smallest_fix: The coordinator writes all seven question lists in one file before wave 1, from the lane table (direction lines 52-61), with no overlap by construction and with the owner's hopes removed. The owner approves them at the first gate. Each child is given its list and not the direction file. This also gives the probe in R1-01 a source that is independent of the child.

findings.title: Cards are checked before anyone knows which cards the review will rest on, by a checker the checked child briefs, against a 95 % gate that punishes a strict checker
findings.argument: The checker opens 'every card that a conclusion will rest on' plus a sample (lines 43-44). That runs at stage A, but the review's conclusions are written in stage B, after gate A has frozen the pack (lines 53-54, 137-138). Cards the review cites that fell outside the sample are never checked, so row 1's 'a checker reopens each card a conclusion rests on' (line 159) has no step that runs it. The checker is a helper of the child (line 21) and its result, CHECK.json, sits in the child's folder (line 113). The checked party chooses the brief and the sample and holds the result. Nobody checks the checker: the coordinator reads no sources (line 19), and the checker is the same model family (Opus) the grading relies on. The gate is also perverse. A card that fails is dropped (lines 45-46), yet gate A still needs at least 95 % of checked cards confirmed (line 53). Below 20 checked cards, one honest failure fails the field and sends it to repair or drop (line 94), so a lenient checker passes where a diligent one fails.
findings.smallest_fix: Replace the 95 % sample gate with a script rule. Every card id cited in pack.md's conclusions, at gate A, and in review.json, at review acceptance, must be listed as confirmed in CHECK.json, and any unconfirmed cited card is checked before the review is accepted. The checker's brief is a fixed file outside the child's folder, and CHECK.json is written in the checker's own folder. Keep the sample's failure count as a ledger measure, not a gate.

findings.title: The synthesis script does not exist and cannot do what the protocol asks of it
findings.target: Amendment 2 row 4; section 6 combination rules; section 8
findings.argument: Row 4 rests the hand-over to the owner on 'the synthesis is built from the review files by a script' (line 162). Section 8 lists only a schema-checking script (line 116), and part C's order of work (lines 187-188) never schedules writing or testing either script. Section 6 asks for two reviews to be 'compared sentence by sentence' (line 79), which no script can do over free prose, and nothing keys reviews so that they can be aligned: each expert picks 'each of our approaches in its field' itself (line 66). When two reviews disagree on a verdict (sound, wrong form, wrong problem, untested), the only remedy is an adjudication in which 'a checker opens the cited sources again' (lines 84-85). That settles a disputed number, not a disputed judgment. Without a script, the coordinator would have to read the reviews itself, which contradicts row 11 (line 174).
findings.smallest_fix: The coordinator fixes an approach list with ids per field, alongside the fixed file list (line 64). review.json keys each verdict by approach id. The synthesis script then compares verdicts per id and writes each disagreement into the owner's table as 'experts disagree', with both reasons and the cards each cited. Adjudication applies only to conflicting card facts. Replace 'sentence by sentence' with this. Writing the schemas, the check script and the synthesis script, and running them on the pilot field's files, becomes the gate between the pilot and wave 1.

findings.title: The second expert's logic assumes the same knowledge; amendment 1 gives it different knowledge, chosen by a coordinator that cannot see the packs
findings.target: Section 6 first bullet; amendment 1 step 4; amendment 2 row 3
findings.argument: Section 6 reasons: 'where two instances with the same knowledge disagree, the claim is weak' (lines 79-80), with the second expert 'from the same pack' (line 78). Amendment 1 step 4 makes the second expert do its own research (lines 140-141), and row 3 relies on that (line 161). The two then hold different cards, so a disagreement may be a gap in research rather than weak judgment, and the stated inference no longer follows. The fields that get a second expert are named 'after gate A' (line 77), by a coordinator that reads no packs (line 174), before any review exists. So the choice of 'fields that decide the next experiment' rests on nothing the coordinator has seen. Each independent second expert is also a whole field run, not a review, and none of the three appears in the waves.
findings.smallest_fix: Pick one form, the owner's call. The cheap form deletes amendment 1 step 4, so the second expert reads the first's frozen pack through R1-03's path and tests judgment, which is what lines 79-80 reason about. The other keeps independent research and rewrites line 80: the script sorts each disagreement into 'cited different cards' (a research gap; check the union) or 'same cards, different verdict' (weak claim). Either way, name the second-expert fields after the reviews are in, from the verdict table, and count them in the waves.

findings.title: The order of work puts the methodologist first and also needs it last, and gives the problem sheet to a coordinator that must not read
findings.target: Part C order of work; section 6 second bullet; section 3 problem sheet
findings.argument: The measurement field runs first, 'because the others are judged by its criteria' (lines 187-188). Its expert, the methodologist, must also review 'every test design the others propose' (line 81), and those exist only after the last wave. Under amendment 1 that expert is a child whose value is its window. Keeping it alive across three or more waves would occupy one of the three slots and keep spending tokens, and stopping it loses the window. Neither choice is stated. The problem sheet, which every expert gets, is 'written by the coordinator from our own measurements' (lines 30-31). The direction gives lane 1 five measurement documents plus 'published cost breakdowns of agents' (direction line 54). Writing that sheet means the coordinator reads sources and large files, which contradicts lines 19 and 174 and grows the coordinator window: the measured main token sink that row 11 exists to prevent.
findings.smallest_fix: The test-design review at the end is done by a fresh session from the methodologist's frozen pack, through R1-03's single path. The problem sheet is the first task of the measurement field's child (or of one helper the coordinator starts). The coordinator only schema-checks it and freezes it before wave 1.

findings.title: The B+ tree section changes no decision except 'split on overflow', which has no limit, no decider and a mid-run cost; the control arm does not measure the tree
findings.argument: 'Balanced' restates three levels, never more (line 15). 'Inner nodes hold keys' restates row 11 (line 174). Neither changes a decision. The one new rule, 'split on overflow' (lines 184-186), has no limit for a question list, does not say who decides, and does not say when. The pack limit (line 49) is checked at gate A, after the child has spent its research budget and holds both halves in its window. A split then throws that window away, or keeps one half in a session that already knows the other, and adds a field to a wave plan already over its count (R1-05). 'A session whose window is full hands over' (line 186) restates amendment 1 step 5. The control arm, 'one field done by a single session without the tree' (lines 189-191), compares against a field that under amendment 1 is already one session. It measures helpers and a checker, not the tree (coordinator, waves, ensembles), on one field, with no scoring rule set in advance.
findings.smallest_fix: Delete the split bullet. An over-limit pack is cut to its limit, with the remainder listed under 'not covered', and a field is split only between waves, by the coordinator, from its question list, before its child starts. Keep 'B+ tree' as a name only. Either name what the control arm scores (which of the seven measures, decided before the run) or drop it.

rows_that_hold.why: A verdict from a closed set, card citations on every factual sentence and 'judgment' marked as such can be checked by the schema script without anyone reading the prose, so it is a real mechanism against raw opinion (lines 66-71).

rows_that_hold.row: Row 3 / section 6 'facts are not voted on'
rows_that_hold.why: A claim stands on a confirmed card, not on agreement. That removes the amplification path for an ensemble of one model regardless of how the second expert is formed (lines 83-84, 161).
Helpers are subagents, and the harness itself does not let a subagent start agents, so the fan-out limit is enforced by the platform and not by goodwill (lines 15, 21, 171).

It runs one field end to end before committing the rest, which is the only place the budget can be grounded. It needs R1-05's admission rule to turn its number into a stop, but the step itself is sound (line 177).

rows_that_hold.row: Section 5 step 3 / row 2 (our work as a fixed file list, no coordinator opinion, 'what would change my mind')
rows_that_hold.why: The coordinator controls the inputs at the review step, so anchoring there is blocked by construction. The leak is earlier, through the question list (R1-07), not here (lines 63-65, 69-70, 160).

No experiments, installs or training, and no project names in searches. Both are simple prohibitions with a clear reader: any search string or install command is visible in the transcript (lines 42-43, 99).
Choosing a folder with no unrelated skills is a one-time act by the coordinator at start, and it cuts the fixed prefix that the owner measured as a main sink for agents (line 175).

rows_that_hold.row: Amendment 1 step 2 (pack written as it goes)
rows_that_hold.why: Writing cards and pack.md incrementally is what makes any recovery from a crash possible at all; R1-03 builds on it (line 134).
It names an ordered step with an effect: findings change the file before the pilot starts (lines 195-196).

result.overall:
I followed one field end to end and the design does not hold. The child writes its own question list from a file that states the owner's hopes. It briefs its own checker. It writes its own exam and answer key, then sits that exam with the key in its window. So the one check meant to show 'the knowledge to be called a proper expert' certifies nothing (R1-01, R1-07, R1-08).

The 300k ceiling, called 'the exception', is crossed in a large share of fields by the protocol's own sizes (R1-02). Together with crash, a failed probe and pack repair, that makes four separate paths back to the builder/expert split that amendment 1 withdrew (R1-03).

Across the whole programme, three checks have no runner: the heartbeat, the PC staying awake and the cap. The coordinator is idle between turns, and usage is read only between waves, so a stall or an overrun goes unseen until the owner returns, which is how the weekly limit was exhausted before (R1-04, R1-05). The shared ledger and source register contradict 'one writer per folder' and per-child branches, and the register defeats independent second experts (R1-06). The synthesis script does not exist and could not compare prose (R1-09).

Most fixes remove or merge rules: one replacement path instead of four, one watcher and status file instead of four wishes, per-folder ledgers instead of a register, coordinator-written question lists, cited cards checked at 100 % instead of a 95 % sample, and dropping the B+ split. What holds: the fixed review form, no voting on facts, the platform-enforced three levels, the pilot field, the lean folder, the incremental pack, and refuting before the pilot.
